sections.section_title: The Complaint and the Crisis of Growth
sections.summary: The community's growth produces a complaint from the Hellenistic Jews that their widows are being overlooked in the daily food distribution; the Twelve summon the congregation and propose a solution, distinguishing between the ministry of the word and the ministry of tables.

sections.section_title: The Selection and Commissioning of the Seven
sections.summary: The community selects seven men -- all with Greek names, led by Stephen who is full of faith and the Holy Spirit -- to oversee the food distribution; the apostles pray and lay hands on them.
The word of God keeps spreading, the number of disciples increases greatly in Jerusalem, and a great many of the priests become obedient to the faith.

sections.section_title: Stephen's Public Ministry and the Dispute
sections.summary: Stephen, full of grace and power, performs great wonders and signs; members of the Synagogue of the Freedmen argue with him but are unable to cope with his wisdom and the Spirit by whom he speaks.

Unable to defeat Stephen in argument, opponents secretly induce false witnesses who charge him with speaking against Moses, God, the temple, and the Law, claiming he said Jesus will destroy the temple and change Moses's customs.

All who sit in the council gaze at Stephen and see his face shining like the face of an angel -- a deliberate allusion to Moses's shining face after receiving the Law at Sinai, ironically confirming Stephen's divine authorization at the moment he is accused of opposing Moses.
